newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-$0.50 lower - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-$0.50 lower - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by continued weakness in pork values, livestock dealers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants could range from $57.00 to $57.50.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range from $55.50 to $56.00 and Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could range from $55.00 to $55.50, dealers there said.
Pork prices were pressured by larger-than-expected hog marketings Monday and projections that runs were large again Tuesday.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog movement Monday totaled 116,000 head, well above that day's estimate of 105,000, USDA said. Tuesday's estimate was 110,000 head.

Carlot pork prices at midday were quoted lower amid moderate supplies and light demand, USDA said. The agency said 33 loads of fabricated cuts and 10.0 loads of pork trimmings had been reported sold at midday.
Tuesday's slaughter was estimated at 369,000 head, bringing the week to date estimate to 700,000, 1.2 percent above a week ago and 1.8 percent above a year ago.
